I am 64 years old and have farmed this land in Quzhou for 45 years. I never went to school, but I know every inch of my 8.5 mu. My household has seven mouths, and some of the younger ones work off-farm in the city, so I cannot take on too much labor-heavy cotton by myself — cotton needs spraying almost every week when the bollworm comes. I will keep 5.5 mu in my reliable wheat-maize rotation, which feeds the family and brings steady grain income, and I will plant 3 mu of cotton for cash. 

For wheat, I trust improved *lumai* seed — it has never let me down. In autumn I rotary-till before sowing, put down compound fertilizer as a basal dose, and topdress with urea at green-up and jointing. With my well I can water four times: the overwintering irrigation, the jointing water, the heading water, and one more at grain-filling if the sky stays dry. I expect about 500 kg per mu. 

For maize, as soon as the wheat is harvested in June I will sow hybrid *denghai* seed directly into the stubble without ploughing — this saves time, keeps moisture, and the wheat straw mulch helps the roots. I give it compound fertilizer at sowing and irrigate twice, at the jointing stage and when the tassels emerge. If the summer rains are normal, two waterings are enough. I look for around 550 kg per mu.

For cotton, I rotary-till in spring and plant improved *guoxin* or *shumian* variety. Cotton needs more fertilizer than grain, especially potash for the bolls, and I must spray for bollworm, aphids, and red spider mite many times through the season — I count on about 16 rounds. I will irrigate twice, at flowering and at peak boll stage. A good year should give me 275 kg of seed cotton per mu.
